turns.content: For a positive integer N, let P(N) be the average of its decimal digits; for example, P(8)=8, P(451)=20, and P(2023)=0. We seek the least positive n satisfying P(n+23)=P(n)+23. Can any one-digit n work?

Now write n=10a+b and consider the case where n and n+23 both have two digits. For 0<=b<=6, adding 23 requires no borrowing from the units digit. Derive P(n+23)-P(n) and state the corresponding legal range of a.
Solve the resulting no-carry digit equation over all legal two-digit pairs, and order the candidate values of n that it produces.
Before declaring the smaller candidate minimal, which one- and two-digit cases still have to be excluded?
Check the remaining two-digit numbers below the smaller candidate for which b=7, 8, or 9 and adding 23 causes no carry. Can any satisfy the equation?
Verify the smaller no-carry candidate directly in P(n+23)=P(n)+23 and state the least positive solution.
